Find constants a project defines in more than one document

Source: R/dict-tools.R
dict_seed.Rd

dict_seed() lists names that two or more documents each assign a literal value, as candidates for dict.yml. It parses the code and never runs it, and it writes nothing.

Usage

dict_seed(paths = NULL, min_files = 2)

Arguments

paths

NULL, or a character vector of files.

min_files

The least number of files that must assign a name, from 1.

Value

A data frame with a row per name: name, value (its text, NA when the values differ), differs, n (files), files and where (every assignment as <file>:<line>: <value>). The attribute skipped is a data frame (file, line, message) of pieces of code that did not parse.

Details

With paths = NULL it reads every .qmd, .Rmd and .rmd file under the project root, except in folders whose name starts with _ or . or is renv. Given paths it reads those files, which may be .R files too; a .R file is read only when named. In a document it reads each r chunk except one with eval = FALSE or another engine in its header, or #| eval: false. A file that is not UTF-8 is read as Latin-1.

A name counts when a top-level expression of a piece (not inside {, if, function or any other call) is name <- literal, name = literal or literal -> name, a literal being a number, a string, - or + of a number, or c() of numbers or of strings with every argument named or none. Logicals, NA, NULL, dates, <<- and assign() do not count.

Limits: a constant written by a computation, or inside a function or a block, is not seen; inline R is not read; a name reused for unrelated things in two documents is listed, and the author decides.
